correctness.rationale: The exact continuous density is derived separately for pairs on the same arm and pairs on distinct arms. Its right intercept and slope recover length and valence. Its distributional second derivative has negative arm atoms and positive pair-sum atoms. After subtracting already recovered shorter arm contributions, the first residual atom is forced to be the next arm, since every pair involving an unrecovered arm is strictly larger. This induction works with arbitrary ties and collisions. The included checker verified 368 exact rational instances and four independent forward-law simulations; they corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The exact distribution of one uniformly sampled point-pair distance is a weak one-dimensional statistic; shape histograms can fail to distinguish general metric-measure spaces. Complete constructive global recovery of all positive arm lengths, including cancellation of edge and pair-sum singularities, is a natural inverse-network geometry theorem beyond general known forward formulas or a generic local-injectivity statement. It does not require a wider tree theorem to be a motivated exact result.
